sourcePageBasis: capture sequence, checked against surrounding folios
paragraphs: Example for flush draw (9 outs) (number of outs)(4) = odds of improving (9)(4) = odds of improving 36% = odds of improving

Bear in mind that the Rule of Four has a maximum absolute error of 3% up to 12 outs. The Rule of Two is slightly less accurate as the number of outs increases. If you're looking for an even more accurate way to estimate your odds of improving, use the modified formula below.
Modified Rule of Two (for turn play)
(number of outs)(2) + [(number of outs)(2)]/10 = odds of improving
Example for flush draw (9 outs) (9)(2) + {(9)(2))/10 = odds of improving 48 + 18/10 = odds of improving 48 + 1.8 = odds of improving 19.8% = odds of improving

All you're doing is calculating your odds of improving using the first formula and then adding 10% of that number. This formula has a maximum absolute erro! of less than 0.9% for up to 19 outs.
